source_snapshot.procedure: Send in-band `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x06 <system-state> <device-state>` on localhost. Source mappings are S0=80, S1=81, S2=82, S3=83, S4=84, S5=85 and no-change=7F; D0=80, D1=81, D2=82, D3=83 and no-change=7F.
source_snapshot.criteria: Command is sent without error and response/state is proper after setting different power states.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes a write but incorrectly says exact raw bytes are missing even though the same row supplies them.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION preserves the byte table and adds one-at-a-time approval, observation and restore, but incorrectly treats the command itself as suspending, hibernating or powering off the host.

old_problem: The historical record retained Pending for selected state matrix, platform support, post-state observation and recovery, and overstated the command as an actual host power transition. IPMI authoritatively defines the complete request grammar and clarifies that this command reports an independently maintained ACPI state to the management controller; it does not itself control or change actual system power. Platform-specific management reactions remain safety-relevant but are parameterizable.
disposition_reason: Preserve every source-listed S0-S5, D0-D3 and 7F mapping as a coverage matrix, but execute only firmware-supported entries whose actual system/device state can be established by an independently approved state-transition workflow. Send each notification one at a time, verify completion and read back the controller's recorded state with Get ACPI Power State 0x07, and monitor platform-management effects. Do not claim that raw 0x06/0x06 itself suspends or powers the host, and do not send a false state merely to exercise a byte.
decision_basis: XLSX row 997, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 998 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 998 / variant faed2e965c6593f4.

IPMI v2.0 section 20.6 says Set ACPI Power State tells a controller the present state and enables reporting; the recorded value is independent of actual system power and the command does not control or change actual power state.

The command can influence elements of the platform-management subsystem, such as fan or sensor handling, and unsupported states may return an error. Confirmation, thermal/management monitoring and a baseline restore are therefore still required even though host power transition is not the command's direct action.

Table 20-7 defines bit 7 as the set/no-change selector, all standard system enumerations, device D0-D3/unknown and completion-only response. The Master provides a valid subset, while 7F must mean no change to one field rather than a substitute for exercising that field.

ED-06, ED-13, ED-15 through ED-19, ED-24, ED-26 through ED-28 and ED-30 preserve state-specific coverage, authorization, evidence and recovery; ED-33 through ED-38 allow supported-state and observer bindings as Project prerequisites without retaining Pending.

test_case.test_name: Notify and verify supported ACPI system/device states over in-band IPMI
test_case.purpose: Verify the bound management controller accepts and records each applicable source-listed ACPI system/device notification, returns the same values through Get ACPI Power State and applies only documented management behavior, without misrepresenting the notification as an actual power-control command.
required_package: Immutable DUT/BMC/local-IPMI mapping, pinned firmware/ipmitool/parser/Script and vendor SDR/firmware documentation identifying supported Set ACPI notifications and management-side effects
Versioned coverage matrix retaining S0=80, S1=81, S2=82, S3=83, S4=84, S5=85, D0=80, D1=81, D2=82, D3=83 and each 7F no-change use, with SPEC-backed N/A for unsupported entries

Independent authoritative actual system/device-state observer and separately approved transition/orchestration for reaching each claimed state; the Set command itself is never counted as that transition
Pre-state Get ACPI 0x06/0x07 readback, management/sensor/fan/thermal/SEL baseline, supported completion map, per-entry timeout and original-state restoration
Protected local execution, maintenance window, workload policy, independent OOB observer and immediate approval for each bounded matrix entry or explicitly approved batch
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED HYBRID MATRIX PROCEDURE ONLY; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Verify the exact target and build the complete source-state applicability matrix. For each supported entry, independently establish or schedule the truthful actual system/device state under its separately approved power-state workflow; capture host/device truth, current 0x06/0x07 recorded state, sensors/fans/thermal/SEL and workload baseline. Immediately before the notification obtain approval, then send exactly one `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x06 <system-byte> <device-byte>` using the source mapping. Require successful IPMI completion with no unexpected response payload, query raw 0x06/0x07 through the independently reviewed paired case, and require matching recorded values while monitoring documented management effects. Use 7F only to hold the other field unchanged and prove it stayed unchanged. Restore the truthful baseline by an approved notification after the actual state workflow returns. Stop on error or unexpected behavior; never sweep, falsify current state, clear logs, trigger a power action as fallback or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: For every applicable matrix entry, the one notification completes successfully, Get ACPI returns the selected reported state for the field whose bit 7 was set and preserves the 7F field, actual system/device state evidence remains independently truthful, and only documented platform-management behavior occurs. Unsupported entries are N/A only with exact platform SPEC evidence; the final reported state and management health match baseline.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS is per matrix entry and for aggregate coverage: exact target/approval, truthful actual-state context, correct source bytes, completion 00, no unexpected response data, exact 0x07 readback, correct 7F preservation, acceptable management/thermal/log behavior and final restoration are mandatory. Command success alone, assuming actual power changed, sending a false state, omitting supported source entries, using 7F as coverage, unproven N/A or borrowing the paired Get verdict fails. Missing support matrix/observer is NOT READY rather than Pending.
safety_gate: Require immediate confirmation for each entry or an explicitly bounded batch after target, truthful current state, workload, OOB observer, thermal safeguards and restore are rechecked.
Do not use 0x06/0x06 to cause or claim an OS sleep/off transition; any real state transition is a separate approved workflow with its own recovery.
Do not notify a state known to be false merely to exercise a byte. Reject unsupported/reserved pairs and preserve every supported source mapping independently.
Monitor fans, sensors, thermals, events and management availability because the controller may alter management behavior based on the reported state; abort on unsafe drift.
Use protected local/verified access, preserve logs and prohibit sshpass, plaintext credentials, host-key bypass and generic log clearing.
No automatic retry, chassis-power fallback or alternate state. Any actual power or management recovery requires separate authorization.
expected_evidence: Approved full source coverage matrix, platform support/N/A specification, DUT/BMC identity and pinned firmware/tool/parser/Script versions
Per-entry approval, independent actual system/device-state truth and pre-notification 0x07 plus sensor/fan/thermal/SEL baseline
Exact request bytes, IPMI completion/response framing and post-notification raw 0x07 decoded readback
Per-entry selected-field match, 7F unchanged proof and timestamped management/thermal/log observations
Final truthful reported-state restoration, no-power-control/no-clear/no-retry audit and independent per-entry plus aggregate verdict
test_case.recovery: If completion, readback or management behavior is unexpected, stop without another notification or power command, retain logs and use the independent observer to protect the platform. After the separately controlled actual-state workflow is safe, the owner may authorize one known-good baseline notification; any fan/thermal, management or actual power recovery follows its dedicated incident runbook and cannot be automated by this case.

source_conflict.reason: The Master command and byte subset are consistent with IPMI notification encoding. Its vague `proper` Criteria is made testable by standard completion plus paired Get readback and documented management behavior; the historical power-control interpretation is corrected rather than treated as source conflict.

blocked.reason: The standard defines command semantics, request bits and response. Platform-supported entries, truthful-state orchestration, expected management effects and restore are finite Project parameters.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: DUT/BMC/local-IPMI binding; firmware/SDR support matrix; truthful actual-state observer/orchestrator; expected management effects; per-entry timeout/approval; 0x07 parser; baseline notification and recovery policy.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; REVIEW-LAYER HYBRID CASE ONLY; NO IPMI, ACPI, FAN, SENSOR, LOG, POWER, HOST OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Section 20.6 and Table 20-7 define notification rather than actual power control, management-side implications, bit-7 set/no-change semantics, state enumerations, completion-only response and unsupported-state errors.

project_authority: The Project owner maps supported actual states and management behaviors for the exact firmware, supplies truthful state orchestration/observation and selects an authorized execution schedule. It cannot redefine the notification as a power-control operation or mark an unsupported entry N/A without platform SPEC evidence.
